concept_code:
import asyncio

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query


class Dispatcher:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.seen: set[str] = set()  # persist this in production
        self.jobs: set[asyncio.Task[None]] = set()

    def receive(self, trigger_id: str, prompt: str) -> bool:
        if trigger_id in self.seen:
            return False  # at-least-once delivery: a redelivered trigger is ignored
        self.seen.add(trigger_id)
        job = asyncio.create_task(self.run(prompt))
        self.jobs.add(job)
        job.add_done_callback(self.jobs.discard)
        return True

    async def run(self, prompt: str) -> None:
        options = ClaudeAgentOptions(tools=[], max_turns=2, max_budget_usd=0.10)
        async for message in query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                print(message.subtype, message.total_cost_usd)

    async def shutdown(self, deadline: float = 30) -> None:
        if self.jobs:
            await asyncio.wait(set(self.jobs), timeout=deadline)
code_focus: `receive()` checks `trigger_id in self.seen` before `asyncio.create_task(self.run(...))`, and `shutdown()` awaits the owned `self.jobs` with `asyncio.wait(..., timeout=deadline)`.

concept_points.title: At-least-once delivery
concept_points.text: Schedulers and webhooks can deliver the same trigger twice, so each id is recorded before work starts.

concept_points.title: Owned background tasks
concept_points.text: Every job task is kept in `self.jobs` until done, so none is garbage-collected or forgotten.

concept_points.title: Graceful shutdown
concept_points.text: Shutdown waits for in-flight `query()` runs up to a deadline instead of killing them halfway.

misconception.claim: Each webhook or cron trigger arrives exactly once, so the handler can just start a run.
misconception.correction: Retries and redeliveries are normal. Without recording trigger ids, the same event starts two paid runs and may repeat side effects.

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query
from nicegui import app, ui


async def explain(prompt: str) -> str:
    """The one lesson service: the HTTP API and the desktop window both call it."""
    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(tools=[], max_turns=1, max_budget_usd=0.05)
    answer = ""
    async for message in query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
        if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.result:
            answer = message.result
    return answer


@app.post("/api/explain")
async def api_explain(prompt: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"answer": await explain(prompt)}


@ui.page("/")
def index() -> None:
    question = ui.input("Prompt")
    output = ui.markdown()

    async def ask() -> None:
        output.content = await explain(question.value)

    ui.button("Ask", on_click=ask)


def launch(desktop: bool) -> None:
    ui.run(native=desktop, window_size=(1200, 800) if desktop else None, reload=False)
code_focus: `explain()` is the single service; `@app.post("/api/explain")` and the `@ui.page("/")` button both call it, and `ui.run(native=desktop)` only chooses between a browser and a pywebview window.

concept_points.text: The FastAPI route and the NiceGUI page call the same `explain()` coroutine, so behaviour cannot drift between them.

concept_points.title: Same async loop
concept_points.text: NiceGUI handlers are async, so they await the SDK's `query()` directly without threads.

misconception.correction: NiceGUI native mode runs the same FastAPI app inside a window. Reusing one service keeps limits, tools and fixes shared.

    return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": str(args["a"] + args["b"])}]}


async def test_add_handler() -> None:
    assert isinstance(add, SdkMcpTool)
    result = await add.handler({"a": 20, "b": 22})
    assert result["content"][0]["text"] == "42"


async def main() -> None:
    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
        tools=[],
        mcp_servers={"calc": create_sdk_mcp_server(name="calc", tools=[add])},
        allowed_tools=["mcp__calc__add"],
        max_turns=3,
    )
    async with ClaudeSDKClient(options=options) as client:
        await client.query("Use the calculator to add 20 and 22.")
        async for message in client.receive_response():
            print(type(message).__name__)
code_focus: `@tool("add", ..., {"a": float, "b": float})` turns the function into an `SdkMcpTool` whose `.handler` is awaited directly in `test_add_handler`, then served with `create_sdk_mcp_server` to `ClaudeSDKClient`.

concept_code:
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Finding(BaseModel):
    path: str
    line: int
    old: str
    new: str


class Review(BaseModel):
    findings: list[Finding]


async def review(diff: str, changed: dict[str, set[int]]) -> list[Finding]:
    review_format = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": Review.model_json_schema()}
    found = Review(findings=[])
    async for message in query(
        prompt=diff, options=ClaudeAgentOptions(tools=[], output_format=review_format)
    ):
        if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output is not None:
            found = Review.model_validate(message.structured_output)
    # Findings are claims: keep only those on lines this PR changed in approved files.
    return [
        item for item in found.findings if item.line in changed.get(item.path, set())
    ]


async def apply_and_test(repo: Path, finding: Finding) -> bool:
    target = repo / finding.path
    target.write_text(
        target.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace(finding.old, finding.new, 1),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    test = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", cwd=repo
    )
    return await test.wait() == 0
code_focus: `review()` validates `structured_output` as `Review` and keeps a `Finding` only if `item.line in changed.get(item.path, set())`; `apply_and_test()` applies the patch and runs pytest in a subprocess.

concept_points.title: Findings are claims

concept_points.title: Scope by changed lines

concept_points.title: Prove with a test
concept_points.text: The host applies the patch itself and accepts it only if the test subprocess exits with code 0.

misconception.claim: If the reviewer agent is confident, its patch can be pushed directly.
misconception.correction: Confidence is not evidence. The host checks scope, applies the patch itself and requires a passing test before publishing.

concept_brief: Red-teaming tests labelled attack cases against deterministic host boundaries rather than trusting the model to refuse. The `decide()` and `inside()` functions in `agent_lab/policy.py` are the same checks the live `can_use_tool` callback and `PreToolUse` `HookMatcher` use, and `redact()` removes keys and bearer tokens from logged data.

A 1.0 pass rate shows the boundary holds whatever text a prompt injection produces.
preparation: Run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/?lesson=74. Offline mode needs nothing else.

`inside()` resolves the path, requires it to stay under the workspace root and rejects any part in `PROTECTED` (.git, .env, .venv, config, .claude); every other tool name falls through to a deny.

quiz.prompt: Why is "shell injection" denied even though the command is harmless `echo preapproved`?

options.text: Because the command text contains a suspicious word.
options.explanation: No. `decide()` does not inspect command text at all.

options.text: Because Bash is not in the read-only lesson policy, so every Bash call is denied.
options.explanation: Correct. Only Read, Glob and Grep can pass; other tools are denied by name.

options.text: Because the model refused it.
options.explanation: No. No model is involved offline; the host decided.

quiz.prompt: What does a red-team pass rate of 1.0 tell you here?

options.text: The model will never follow injected instructions.
options.explanation: No. The cases test host boundaries, not model behavior.

options.text: The app is fully secure.
options.explanation: No. It only covers these labelled cases; add more as new attacks appear.

options.text: Every labelled case got the host decision it was expected to get.
options.explanation: Correct. `pass_rate` is the share of rows where `allowed == expected`.

code_focus: `CASES` labels five attacks with expected outcomes, `pass_rate()` runs them through `decide()`, and `gate` uses that same `decide()` as the live `can_use_tool` callback.

concept_points.title: Labelled attack cases
concept_points.text: Each case names an attack, the tool call it produces and whether the host should allow it.

concept_points.title: Deterministic boundary
concept_points.text: `decide()` resolves paths and rejects traversal, `.env` and non-read tools, whatever text a prompt injection contains.

concept_points.title: Same check in production
concept_points.text: The tested `decide()` is exactly what `can_use_tool` calls, so a 1.0 pass rate describes the live boundary.

misconception.claim: Red-teaming means checking that the model refuses malicious prompts.
misconception.correction: Refusals vary between runs and models. Red-team tests should target deterministic host checks that hold even when the model complies.

concept_brief: An autonomous engineering team works when agents propose and the host decides. In live mode `run_live_team` in `agent_lab/engineering.py` runs a lead, two parallel developers and a reviewer through `query()` with `output_format` JSON schemas (`Plan`, `DevelopmentReport`, `TeamReview`); the host validates file ownership and dependencies, checks source with an AST allowlist, runs acceptance tests in an isolated `python -I` subprocess, tracks spend with `Budget` and decides the release gate.

It shows the whole control loop, ending in a host release gate and no publication, without any model call.

quiz.prompt: In live mode, how does the host stop a developer agent from running arbitrary code?

options.text: It trusts the reviewer agent to catch it.

options.text: It gives the agent Bash but no network.

options.text: It checks the proposed source with an AST allowlist before writing or running it.

concept_points.text: Lead, developers and reviewer return structured proposals through `output_format`, validated with `model_validate`.

misconception.claim: A team of agents that reviews its own work can decide when to release.
misconception.correction: Agents can agree on a wrong answer. The host checks ownership, runs tests, tracks budget and makes the release decision itself.
